arguments.ask: Post about what we ship. Every merged PR, LinkedIn only, one post each.
arguments.context: Developer tool for small teams; the founder posts on LinkedIn.

steps.why: The planner can plan routines fed by an app; create-routine can't find a GitHub connection. It returned a plan for each merged pull request with LinkedIn and X, 2 posts each, and needs: 'Connect GitHub' with a link to bolta.ai/dashboard/connections. App-fed routines are switched on per brand: elsewhere plan answers status refused, "not available for this brand yet"; say so and offer weekly posts from a changelog page instead.
The user already said LinkedIn only and one post each: exact fields, no guessing. It returns a new plan id; the old one can no longer be saved.

say: Here's the plan: each time a pull request is merged, Bolta writes 1 LinkedIn post about what changed and why it matters; dependency bumps and other routine merges are skipped. Each waits for your yes and uses credits. First connect GitHub here: bolta.ai/dashboard/connections. Tell me when it's done and I'll save it, switched off.
never: confirm-plan before GitHub is connected: it is refused as plan_not_ready.
Inventing a connection id in create-routine source_bindings.
Saying it runs every week: it runs on each merge.
